Prevention: Transplant only healthy seedlings to new fields and site nurseries away from tomato fields to reduce seedling infections
Thrips are the main vector in the transmission of
TSWV, in nurseries plants can be covered with with a fine mesh (sizes smaller than 0.5mm) to prevent access to the thrips.
Alternatively chemical pesticides can be used to control the vectors (see yellow control column)
Control weeds on the fields (and around fields) and all volunteer crops - TSWV has many different hosts
Mulch field with dry grass to prevent pupation of thrips
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: pepper, tobacco, irish potato

Monitor field regularly to detect early symptoms of the disease - look for bronzing and curling of the leaves, nectrotic streaks or spots on the leaves and leaf stalks, stunting of the whole plant and ringspots on fruit
Also monitor regularly for signs of thrips on surfaces of leaves in the nursery and field, consider chemical control if populations are high
TSWV is one of the most economically devastating diseases of tomato therefore, action to control it should start soon after symptoms are observed
Direct Control: Rogue early infected plants at very low disease incidence and destroy by burning
Spray alpha-cypermethrin at 7.5ml/15L of water to control the vector population.
A contact and ingested pyrethroid insecticide, IRAC group: 3A
Spray field with imidacloprid at 5-7ml/15L of water to control thrip and other insect vectors, if vector populations persist.
A systemic neonicotinoid insecticide, IRAC group: 4A
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
The virus can not be manged using pesticides but the insect vector can be controlled using insecticides:
Apply three times at 7-14 days intervals depending on vector situation.
Alternate with other chemical group insecticides after three applications.
Apply three times at intervals of 7-14 days depending on vector population.
Alternate with other chemical group insecticides after three applications.
